title: From Vibe Coding To Vibe Engineering – Kitze, Sizzy
talk_summary: Kitze's talk is mostly a comedic rant contrasting 'vibe coding' (accept blindly) with 'vibe engineering' (steer agents with technical context, rules, and skepticism). The few concrete mechanisms are: tight human-in-the-loop watching of fast agents, rich context/rules/memory files, voice-driven brain-dump feedback, and the claim that skeptical seniors get 10x while juniors should not be given agents.

takeaways.what_they_do: Maintains explicit rules, docs, commands, and memory so the agent has app context instead of guessing; says without it you fail most of the time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use rules, docs, commands, and memories... without the right context, you will like fail most of the time

takeaways.technique: Technical-jargon prompts instead of vague 'fix it' prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: Writes prompts naming specific abstractions, patterns, and files to change (e.g. TRPC procedure definitions) rather than 'make no mistakes'.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's like a bunch of technical jargon and it's never like fix the app

takeaways.technique: Human watches agent execution live and interrupts
takeaways.what_they_do: With fast agents he stays in the driver's seat, watching the diff/UI and stopping the agent mid-run when it goes wrong, instead of waiting for a finished result.
After an agent finishes, he narrates what he sees in the UI and code out loud, producing a detailed thinking-process transcript used as the next prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I explain what I see in the UI as if I'm talking to a friend... I'm literally seeing my thinking process out loud

takeaways.technique: Route work by skill tier: seniors steer agents, juniors don't
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues the 10x comes from skeptical senior engineers driving agents; giving agents to juniors/interns is the dumbest idea because they can't judge correctness.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Do not give AI tools to your interns and juniors... if you take your skeptical senior and you convince them to do vibe engineering, you're going to get 10x results

takeaways.technique: Accept 'good enough' code; avoid premature abstraction
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues LLMs don't care about repetitive code and that over-abstraction creates roadblocks; the valuable skill is judging which code is good enough for its job.
